mustKeepText: Shift sequences for a sniffed Japanese charset
expect.notes: Found by the html-3 bypass review. If the frame were ever read as ISO-2022-JP (no charset declared, the browser guesses), ESC $ B makes the following bytes two-byte characters and can swallow a closing quote, so the next attribute value would be read as attributes (onerror). The sanitizer turns ESC into U+FFFD everywhere and the document declares UTF-8 within its first 1,024 bytes.

title: Image functions whose address comes from a variable, an attribute or the environment

mustKeepText: Stylesheet values that are filled in later
expect.notes: Found by the html-3 bypass review. var(), env() and attr() are filled in after the sanitizer has read the stylesheet, so inside image-set(), image() and src() they could put a string the sanitizer never classified in URL position (a relative img/<n> or cid/<n> on the frame's own origin, or a remote address). They are replaced inside image functions; address-like strings are emptied everywhere, and url() in a custom property is rewritten like any other (the one remote image left: img/0 through the proxy when images are on).

title: A frameset fallback whose tags rebuild themselves each time one is removed

mustKeepText: A frameset fallback that rebuilds itself
expect.notes: Found by the Opus review of html-3. The sanitizer re-parses <noframes> text as markup; once it also removed nested <noframes> tags in one pass, <nofr<noframes>ames> became <noframes> again, and each level re-read everything below it with fresh limits (quadratic). Fallbacks are now re-parsed only at the top level, one inside re-parsed text is dropped, and all re-parses share one element budget. The bigger shape is timed in tests/perf.test.ts.

expect.notes: From the Integrator's round-2 review of html-3. Aplos's own wrappers carry classes that start aplos-, and a mail class of that name is moved to m-aplos-. The selectors here reached the wrappers by a dot, a comment and a name, by [class] attribute selectors with every operator, quoting and flag, and inside :is(), :where(), :not() and :has() (also malformed ones); each now names m-aplos- instead. The oracle in tests/oracle.ts fails any sanitized corpus message whose CSS still names an aplos- class. Tag and position selectors (details, p:last-child) can still hide a wrapper: cosmetic, recorded in DECISIONS.

title: A class selector whose value is an address, with an aplos- name beside it

A [class=...] string that holds an aplos- name is rewritten (aplos- to m-aplos-), and the rewritten value was first written without the checks every other string gets: an address-like string was kept, and inside image-set(), -webkit-image-set() or image() the value skipped URL classification. Now the rewritten value is judged as written: an address-like string is emptied, and inside an image function it goes through the image book (here none, because a name in front makes it relative). The oracle fails any message that still carries an address.

title: Lengths in viewport units on the root, in custom properties, calc() and escapes

mustKeepText: Viewport units sized this letter to its own frame
expect.notes: From the ui-core REQUEST (html-5 slice 2). The frame is sized to the letter, so a letter sized by 100vh grew the frame, which grew the letter, without end (a 7.6 GB renderer in the host's browser spec). Every vw/vh/vi/vb/vmin/vmax length, also the s/l/d forms, in escapes, calc(), min(), max(), clamp(), custom properties, media and supports preludes and style attributes, becomes px against a fixed reading viewport (640 x 600), clamped to 100,000 px. The oracle fails any sanitized message that still holds one; the browser run checks that this message's height settles.

title: Names and ids on every member the frame's script reads, on every element that can carry one

mustKeepText: Every member of document, window and an element

expect.notes: From the ui-core REQUEST (html-5 slice 2). A named img, form, embed, object or iframe shadows document.body, documentElement, addEventListener and the rest on document; an id shadows window members that are inherited from EventTarget. The sanitizer drops form, embed, object, iframe, frameset, select, textarea, button, svg and math, keeps name only on a, and moves every id and name to m-<name>, which is not a JavaScript identifier. The oracle fails any name or id outside m-. The reporter also takes its members from the prototypes before the mail can matter; the browser run loads this message and an unsanitized copy and checks the report.

title: A comment and a 3.2 doctype before the real one, and a table that wants to be window-tall

The first doctype the mail declared used to decide the frame's rendering mode, and most mail declares none or an old one, so most frames laid out in quirks mode, where body.scrollHeight follows the viewport. The document now always starts with <!DOCTYPE html> (tests pin the first bytes of the served document, and the browser run checks document.compatMode).

title: Container query units with no container, in escapes, calc(), custom properties and style attributes

mustKeepText: Container units fall back to the viewport
expect.notes: From the independent review of the frame reporter fixes. cqw, cqh, cqi, cqb, cqmin and cqmax resolve against the small viewport when no ancestor is a size container, which is how the sanitizer's own output is laid out, so 100cqh grew the frame exactly like 100vh (132 to 4,900 px, then the 300-report cap in the browser run). They are rewritten to px like the viewport units (css.ts viewportLength), also with a container declared: the mail cannot be relied on to declare one, and a declared size container could still be sized by the frame. container-type and container are left alone. The oracle fails any sanitized CSS that still holds a cq unit; reporter.e2e.ts checks that the frame settles.

title: !important rules in the mail's own layers, named, ordered and anonymous

mustKeepText: A layered !important rule beats an unlayered one
expect.notes: From the Integrator's review of PR #249 (reading CSS). Vector 4: a layered !important declaration beats an unlayered !important one, so the unlayered reading rules lost to @layer x{html{height:calc(100% + 50px)!important}}. The reading rules now live in the first declared layer, whose !important wins over every later layer, unlayered rules and a style attribute.

title: An inline body style with position:fixed !important, and an html style

expect.notes: Vector 5 of the Integrator's REQUEST, with !important on every offset. The body's style attribute survives on the frame's body, and an element's own style attribute outranks every cascade layer (element-attached styles rank before layers), so an inline !important beat the layered reading rule. The frame body's style now keeps only background*, color, margin*, padding*, font*, text-align and line-height (css.ts keepDeclarations, sanitize.ts BODY_STYLE_PROPERTIES), so it cannot touch anything the layer guards; the oracle fails any other property there.

title: Mail layers named aplos-reading (plain, escaped, dotted, in a statement, after a comment, inside @media)

title: A div and the body whose style attributes differ only by a leading marker

mustKeepText: The body then asks for the same declarations
expect.notes: From the second independent review of the reading layer. HIGH: the body's filtered style was cached under '!' + its text while every other element's unfiltered style was cached under the bare text, so a div with style="!x;P" planted its unfiltered result under the key a later <body style="x;P"> looked up, and the body kept position:fixed!important and zoom:1000!important (268 reports, 650 to 13,800 px, still growing). The body's style is no longer cached at all (sanitize.ts bodyStyle); the other caches (styleTokens, hidingStyles, cleanStyles) are each keyed by the style text for one transformation, images.ts keeps separate maps per kind.

title: Vertical Japanese text under -epub-writing-mode and other prefixed aliases

mustKeepText: Aliases of writing-mode turn a block sideways
expect.notes: From the second independent review of the reading layer. MEDIUM: Chromium honours -epub-writing-mode (and -webkit-writing-mode) as aliases of writing-mode, and only the unprefixed and -webkit- names were renamed; the -epub- block hit the host's 303-report cap (632 to 5,400 px). Every property whose name ends in writing-mode, under any prefix, escape or case, becomes a custom property. Measured: text-orientation, text-combine-upright, glyph-orientation-vertical, direction with unicode-bidi, -webkit-line-break and -webkit-box-orient settle on their own (no vertical mode without writing-mode).

title: A body style with a 3,000 px font, a line height of 100 and a 900 px font shorthand

mustKeepText: Huge type on the body is left out
expect.notes: From the second independent review of the reading layer. LOW: the body style's font-*, margin-* and padding-* were prefix patterns, so font-size-adjust:1000 (16,917 px) or a huge font-size or line-height (8,566 px) passed: stable but tall. The allowlist is now explicit names, and font-size, line-height and font are bounded (200 px or the equivalent in other units, a unitless line height of 10, no functions); margin and padding are not bounded (a spacer div can be as tall).

title: CSS if() with media() conditions on the frame's height, shape and orientation

expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (CSS if() and the clipped-content measurement). CSS if() takes media() conditions, and Chromium 137 and later evaluates them: padding-top:if(media(max-height:300px):600px;else:0) brought back the endless flip the @media rewrite stops (217 reports in 3.5 s, 564 and 164 px). if( is now dropped like attr(: the function becomes an empty string, the declaration is invalid and ignored, in style blocks, style attributes and inside calc() or var(). Container queries on min-block-size and max-block-size are renamed like the other height features.

title: The allowlisted body margin carrying an if(media()) condition

mustKeepText: The body margin asks the frame which way up
expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (CSS if() and the clipped-content measurement). The same vector through the body's style attribute, which keeps margin and padding by name (786 and 86 px, 217 reports). The function is dropped before the declaration is written.

title: A height keyframe tied to the scroll or view timeline

expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (CSS if() and the clipped-content measurement). animation-timeline:scroll(root) ties an animation's progress to the scroller, which is the frame, so the keyframe's height was in effect only when the frame could scroll: the letter flipped between 86 and 1086 px (217 reports in 3.5 s). The timeline properties (animation-timeline, animation-range*, scroll-timeline*, view-timeline*, timeline-scope) become custom properties, and scroll() and view() are dropped as functions. Ordinary animations and transitions are untouched.

title: display:contents on the body, and a box positioned 1,200 px down

mustKeepText: A body with no box is no containing block
expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (CSS if() and the clipped-content measurement). With display:contents the body had no box, position:relative made no containing block, and the report was 54 against a true 1,224. The body rule now sets display:block with !important in the reading layer.

title: An absolutely positioned box that moves 1,200 px down a second after load

mustKeepText: Nothing changes size, so no observer fires
expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (CSS if() and the clipped-content measurement). The ResizeObserver watched only the root, whose box does not change when an absolute box moves, and the report stayed at 86 against a true 1,224. The reporter now looks at every frame for 3 s after any change or event (animationend, transitionend, load, error, toggle, resize), posts only a changed report and at most 20 a second, and observes the body as well. A move more than 3 s after the last change, with no event, is not seen (recorded in DECISIONS).

title: An absolutely positioned box that jumps 1,200 px down a second after load and animates for 100 s

mustKeepText: The jump has no end event
expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (the clipped-content measurement). Like 171 but the animation does not end for 100 s, so no animationend event can report it: only the reporter's look at every frame after a change sees the jump.

title: An absolutely positioned box that starts moving 4.5 s after load

mustKeepText: Nothing moves until the frame loop has gone quiet
expect.notes: From the independent review of #255 (the clipped-content measurement). The frame loop stops after 3 s without a change; a box that starts moving later is reported when its animation ends (the animationend event, captured on the document). A late move with no end event, a long or infinite animation that starts after the quiet period, is not seen and is recorded in DECISIONS.

title: A body whose background colour animates for ever

expect.notes: From the Integrator's review of #257 and the old Engine thread's re-check (reporter lifetime). A letter that changes only colour posted a report for as long as it was open (about 23 a second, 40 in 5 s at a 2 s cycle): the background rode in the change key and every post extended the watch, and the host's freeze counts only growth. The background is no longer a reason to post (it still rides in every message) and only a new height or width extends the watch, so this letter posts its first report and its readiness and then nothing.

title: A box whose height animates for ever

expect.notes: From the Integrator's review of #257 and the old Engine thread's re-check (reporter lifetime). A size that changes for the life of the letter is limited to 20 reports a second and, after 2,000 reports in all, the reporter posts the state of that moment and stops for good (the host keeps that size). The browser check shortens the cap to 60 in a copy of the script to see it in seconds.
